_what: A whole look generated from three inputs (tools/screen-looks/read-data/theme-from-inputs.ts): `base` (the colour of the page: its lightness picks light or dark and its hue and chroma tint every ground and ink), `accent` (the colour of the actions: only its hue and chroma are kept) and `contrast` (0 to 100: how far ink moves from the ground). Every token below is derived in OKLCH, a space where equal lightness steps look equal, then pulled inside the sRGB gamut so no browser clips it, then checked against `floors`: if ink and ground are closer than a floor, the ink is moved away from the ground (the other way when that side has no room) until the floor holds. `roles` are rows: an `id` (floors name roles by it), the `tokens` of the look it sets (the compact keys and the css-named keys looks use, whichever the look has), which input tints it (`base` or `accent`), and per scheme the lightness at contrast 0 and at contrast 100 (it moves in a straight line between), the most chroma it may carry and the least (`chroma_min`, accent roles only: a dull pick still reads as a colour). A token the look lacks is skipped. A pick with chroma under `neutral_below` has no hue and is treated as grey on purpose. A new role or floor is a row here.

words.bad_contrast: Contrast is a number from {min} to {max}.
